scope.instruction: Fully static Astro 7 site: every page is prerendered at build time and served as static files by nginx (Dockerfile). No SSR, no API routes, no backend. Known attacker-reachable inputs: (1) Ghost CMS post HTML injected via set:html in src/pages/blog/[...slug].astro — evaluate XSS impact if the CMS is compromised; (2) the contact form in src/pages/contact.astro posts to the external FormSubmit.co service (honeypot _honey field, _captcha disabled); (3) localStorage-based dark mode script in BaseLayout.astro; (4) URLs listed in src/data/portfolio.ts. Critical invariant to verify: the Ghost Content API key (env CONTENT_API_KEY, GHOST_URL) used at build time must NOT leak into any client-visible output in dist/ (JS bundles, HTML, sitemap). src/components/ui/** is vendored shadcn-vue components mostly unused by pages — deprioritize but report if reachable. Also review Dockerfile/nginx static serving configuration (docker/nginx.conf) and the Astro/Vite build configuration in astro.config.mjs.

WHITE-BOX validation of a CRITICAL invariant on repo /workspace/portfolio-astro (Astro 7 static site, build-time Ghost credentials).

Invariant to verify: the build-time secrets GHOST_URL and CONTENT_API_KEY (declared via astro:env in astro.config.mjs, context "server", access "secret"; consumed in src/lib/ghost.ts; passed as Docker --build-args in Dockerfile) must NOT appear in ANY client-visible artifact:
1. Existing build output dist/: grep every file (HTML, JS/CSS under dist/_astro/, sitemap-index.xml/sitemap.xml, robots.txt, favicons) for the actual secret values. Read /workspace/portfolio-astro/.env to obtain the real values for grep purposes — but NEVER echo the actual key value into any note, report, message, or artifact; refer to it only as "<CONTENT_API_KEY value>" and match via grep -F with the value supplied from the shell without printing it.
2. dist/.prerender or any server-side chunks in dist/ (the Dockerfile deletes dist/.prerender before the nginx stage — verify such chunks exist in a build and confirm what they contain and that deletion logic is correct/complete; also check whether any OTHER non-public files survive into dist/).
3. Source maps: check whether any .map files are emitted into dist/ and whether they embed source or env values.
4. Fresh rebuild: run `bun install --frozen-lockfile` if needed and `bun run build` in /workspace/portfolio-astro (local execution is authorized; write the new build to dist/ as normal), then re-run all dist checks on the fresh output. Also verify .env is not copied into dist/ by any public-dir copying.
5. Git history exposure: run gitleaks over the repo INCLUDING history (or `git log -p --all | grep` for the key value / GHOST_URL) to check the secret was never committed. .git is a read-only mount — do not attempt writes.
6. Docker build-context exposure: read .dockerignore and confirm .env, .git, strix_runs, dist are excluded from `COPY . .` in the Dockerfile; identify anything sensitive that WOULD be copied into the build image layers (note: docker is not available in the sandbox, so analyze statically).
7. Sitemap check: confirm sitemap URLs contain only public pages (no secret query params like ?key= on any Ghost asset URLs, no internal URLs).
8. Check how GHOST_URL/CONTENT_API_KEY could ever surface client-side: any use of import.meta.env.*, PUBLIC_-prefixed env, astro:env client context, or JSON serialization into page props / ViewTransitions data / island props.

The shared threat model is saved for "https://portfolio.aplix.nl" — call get_threat_model first.

Closure discipline: each of the 8 checks ends as confirmed (leak found — then immediately spawn a validation child if needed, and a reporting child to file create_vulnerability_report with the fix inline), ruled_out (name the specific control, e.g. astro:env access:secret semantics + grep results showing absence, .dockerignore entry), or needs_follow_up. Record coverage for surface="build output secret leakage (CONTENT_API_KEY/GHOST_URL)" risk_area="build-time secret exposure". Write a shared note (category: findings or methodology) summarizing results.

IMPORTANT safety: never write the real secret value into notes/reports/final messages; describe matches as "the value from .env matched file X" with redacted excerpts.

WHITE-BOX + DYNAMIC assessment of the contact form in /workspace/portfolio-astro/src/pages/contact.astro, which POSTs from visitors' browsers to the external FormSubmit.co service (no backend exists). Deployed at https://portfolio.aplix.nl.

SCOPE (yours only): the contact form and everything it exposes:
1. Static analysis of src/pages/contact.astro: every form field and hidden input (`_captcha`, `_honey`, `_next`, `_template`, `_subject`, hidden email/recipient fields?), the action URL (which FormSubmit endpoint form — plain form endpoint vs ajax), method, client-side validation, how the honeypot is implemented (CSS-hidden? JS-removed?), whether any token/recipient address is disclosed in the HTML, autocomplete attributes, and any tracking IDs.
2. Research current FormSubmit.co behavior via web_search/web_get_contents: which special fields are honored client-side (`_next`, `_subject`, `_template`, `_captcha`, `_cc`, `_bcc`, `_replyto`, custom headers), whether a plain form endpoint allows overriding the recipient, and known abuse patterns.
3. Dynamic tests (keep it MINIMAL and labeled — at most 2-3 real submissions to the live endpoint, subject clearly marked "[SECURITY-TEST portfolio scan]"; do not spam):
   a. CSRF: confirm the form can be POSTed cross-origin from an attacker page (no token exists) — demonstrate with a local HTML page that auto-submits to the live endpoint and observe the submission being accepted. Assess honest impact (unsolicited mail to the owner as the victim's visitor identity; no auth/session exists on this site).
   b. Special-field injection: replay the live form POST via Caido repeat_request adding `_subject` (incl. CRLF/header-injection variant), `_next=https://example.invalid` (open-redirect-after-submit), `_template=table/raw` variants, and observe/verify what FormSubmit accepts (HTTP response codes/JSON). WHITE-BOX + DYNAMIC assessment of deployment/serving configuration for /workspace/portfolio-astro (fully static Astro site served by nginx in Docker) at https://portfolio.aplix.nl.

SCOPE (yours only):
1. docker/nginx.conf — review every directive against live behavior: security header set (nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS — note HSTS is emitted on port 80 which browsers ignore until received over TLS: verify what the live HTTPS responses actually carry), missing CSP, `add_header` inheritance gotcha (any `location` with its own add_header silently DROPS the parent server-level headers in nginx — check robots.txt, sitemap-index.xml, /_astro/ locations on the LIVE site for missing security headers; this is a real nginx semantics bug to verify dynamically), try_files behavior, error_page 404 internal handling, caching policies, MIME/nosniff behavior.
2. Dockerfile + .dockerignore — build hygiene: secrets as build args (recorded in image history — verify statically since docker is unavailable; assess whether GHOST_URL/CONTENT_API_KEY being ARG/ENV risks layer/history leak and whether build-secret mounts would be better), COPY . . exposure (what gets copied: check .dockerignore vs repo contents incl. strix_runs/, .env, .git), multi-stage correctness (dist/.prerender deletion — coordinate: another agent owns deep secret-leak checks, you only review the mechanism), nginx:alpine pinning (unpinned tag), root user defaults, EXPOSE 80.
3. Live nginx behavior tests (targeted, through the proxy): encoded path traversal attempts (/%2e%2e/, /..;/, /%2e%2e%2f etc. — verify 404, no file served), dotfile serving (/.env, /.git/HEAD — expect 404; coordinate with live-recon note to avoid duplication, just verify), method handling (TRACE/OPTIONS/PUT), directory listing on any path with and without trailing slash, Host-header sensitivity (Host: localhost / arbitrary — observe response differences), HTTP→HTTPS redirect on the actual port 80 endpoint if reachable, and sitemap/robots behavior. Capture Caido request IDs for anything anomalous.
4. astro.config.mjs — build config review: sitemap() site URL correctness, env schema handling (secret leakage is another agent's job — you only note config-level risks), vite config, output mode confirmation (static).
5. public/robots.txt content sanity (no accidental disallow of everything, no internal URLs).

Severity honesty: missing-header/caching findings on a static personal portfolio are Low/Info unless a concrete exploit path exists; a header-drop caused by add_header inheritance that removes HSTS/nosniff on asset responses is still low but worth reporting as a config bug with the nginx-semantic root cause explained. Only file a report (via a reporting child: create_agent, skills=["vulnerabilities/information_disclosure","vulnerabilities/header_injection"]) when there is a demonstrable security consequence; include the inline fix (nginx.conf fix_before/fix_after, e.g. repeating headers inside each location or using `headers-more`/include pattern) with fix_verification reasoning.
